$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for all ISO 19650 code tables used by Planscape training, templates and docs. Edit here only. Run `node cpd/build.mjs` to regenerate outputs and `node cpd/validate.mjs` to check the repo for drift.
governingRule: Where this data and a project's BIM Execution Plan disagree, the BEP wins. These tables are the most widely used default set, not law.

parties.name: Appointing party
parties.usually: The client — university, ministry, developer, owner
parties.does: Commissions the work. Issues the EIR. Receives and accepts the information.

parties.name: Lead appointed party
parties.does: Responds to the EIR with a BEP. Coordinates the appointed parties. Compiles the MIDP. Answerable for the whole information deliverable.

parties.name: Appointed party
parties.does: Produces information for its own task, to a TIDP. Answerable to the lead appointed party.

requirementChain.name: Organizational Information Requirements
requirementChain.question: What information does this organisation need to run itself?

requirementChain.name: Asset Information Requirements
requirementChain.question: What do we need to know about the asset in operation?

requirementChain.name: Project Information Requirements
requirementChain.question: What must this project tell us, to decide at each stage?

requirementChain.name: Exchange Information Requirements
requirementChain.question: What exactly is handed over, at this exchange, in what form?
requirementChain.setBy: Appointing party to lead appointed party

nameFields.name: Project
nameFields.notes: 3-6 characters. Fixed for the life of the project.

nameFields.name: Originator
nameFields.notes: 3-4 characters. Not the individual, and not the discipline - the firm.

nameFields.name: Volume/System
nameFields.notes: ZZ = whole project. Use zone codes only where the project defines them.

nameFields.name: Level/Location
nameFields.notes: ZZ = all levels, XX = not applicable. Otherwise per the BEP.

nameNotFieldsNote: Suitability and revision are metadata attributes that travel with the container in the CDE. Some firms append them to filenames as a local convenience; that is not part of the required name.

roleCodesLocal.name: Fire protection
roleCodesLocal.note: Common local addition. Legitimate provided the BEP defines it.

typeCodes.name: Drawing
typeCodes.warn: A drawing is DR even when produced from a model. M3 is the model file itself.

cdeStates.name: Shared
cdeStates.write: The author, by publishing into it
cdeStates.holds: Issued for coordination, information or review

cdeStates.name: Published
cdeStates.write: Only the authorised approver, under the approval process

cdeStates.name: Archived
cdeStates.holds: The historical record. Every superseded revision.

suitability.question: What may the recipient DO with this?
suitability.variationNote: Codes above S4 vary between national annexes and project protocols in number and wording. Some projects use them; many do not. Check the BEP.

codes.recipientMay: Nothing. Not for issue. Sits in WIP.
Position and design their own work against it. Expect it to change.
Be aware of it. Not an invitation to design against.
Approve or reject at a stage gate.

authorization.question: Was this accepted, and with what qualification?

codes.detail: Authorised for the stated purpose. The number denotes purpose or stage, per the BEP.
Authorised, but the originator must address the comments at the next revision.

codeFamilyRule: S codes describe the suitability of SHARED information. A and B codes describe the authorization status of PUBLISHED information. They coexist; a container does not carry both at once. A drawing shared for coordination is S1. That same drawing, approved and published, is A1.
revisionRule: Crossing from P into C restarts the numbering under the new letter. A drawing at P03 issued for construction for the first time becomes C01, not P04.

cdeTests.test: State transitions exist and are enforced - you cannot drag a file into Published
cdeTests.ifFails: The status of every file is a matter of opinion

cdeTests.test: Access control is tied to state - nobody can overwrite approved information
cdeTests.ifFails: Contract-grade information is one careless drag from being lost

cdeTests.test: There is an audit trail - you can answer who approved this, and when
cdeTests.ifFails: You cannot defend a submission that is challenged

cdeTests.test: Suitability and revision travel with the container
cdeTests.ifFails: Nobody downstream knows what they may do with it

cdeTests.test: There is a single source of truth - one authoritative version
cdeTests.ifFails: Teams coordinate against different versions and clashes never converge

selfAudit.q: Does the project have a BEP - and has anyone read it in the last three months?
Can you produce a MIDP showing every deliverable, its owner and its date?
Do containers carry compliant names, consistently - including the ones produced last week?
Are there four distinct CDE states with enforced permissions - not four folders anyone can write to?
Does every shared container carry a suitability code, and every published one an authorization code?
Could you show an auditor who authorised the current published revision of any given drawing, and when?

selfAuditRule: Score honestly, not generously. A fail on any critical question means the project is not running an ISO 19650 information management process, whatever the BEP claims.

midpMinimumRow.label: The deliverable
midpMinimumRow.why: what container is to be produced

bepMustSettle: The information delivery strategy and how it responds to the EIR
Roles and responsibilities, including who performs information management
Standards, methods and procedures - including the naming convention and the code tables this project uses
The CDE: platform, states, permissions, transition and approval process
The coordinate system and units - agreed once at mobilisation, never changed
The MIDP, or a commitment to produce one and when
Quality assurance and model validation - how compliance is checked, by whom, how often
commonMistakes: Calling the client the lead appointed party. They are the appointing party.
Listing suitability or revision as a field in the container name. They are metadata.
Naming a drawing M3. A drawing is DR, even when generated from a model.
Inventing a zone code when the project is not subdivided. Use ZZ.
Issuing at S2 what you meant to issue at S1 - or the reverse.
Putting an S code on published information. Published carries A or B.
Going P03 to P04 when the drawing has gone to construction. It becomes C01.
Calling a shared folder a CDE because the filenames are tidy.
Writing a BEP once, filing it, and never opening it again.

glossary.means: Asset Information Model - the information set for the asset in operation
Any named, structured set of information - a model, drawing, schedule, document
Project Information Model - the information set produced during delivery
What a recipient may do with shared information
A group delivering a defined package of information
